newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - New issues and more to come.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - New issues and more to come.

text.p: The Eurobond market's new issues calendar is again chock full of Brazilian names, following the placement of more than $4.0 billion in new Brazilian paper last week.
** Safra leasing, a unit of Banco Safra, issued a $150 million eight-year bond, with puts and calls at three and five years, early Monday through Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Bear Stearns.
The bond was expected to price later at 175-185 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.

** Grupo Votorantim was seen joining Safra this week, when it should issue its $300 million eight-year bond. It will be the group's first deal, with wide-ranging price talk of between 180-220 bps. ING Bank is lead manager for the deal which should come Tuesday.
The bond, which has been in the works for months, will be guaranteed by five companies in the group, including Votorantim Celulose e Papel.

** Sao Paulo electricity company Cesp was also expected to issue its long-delayed $200 million 10-year bond, with puts and calls after five years. The deal is being led by J.P. Morgan and was expected to come at a spread of between 260-280 bps.
Debt watchers said the flood of new Brazilian paper was not dampening investor appetite for the nation's debt.
"All the new stuff is being absorbed really well. New issues last week tightened by five basis points on average," said a Eurobond trader in Sao Paulo.
THE BUSY NEW ISSUES schedule follows more than $4.0 billion in new Brazilian debt placed last week.
Brazil's $3.0 billion 30-year global ZYDC, of which $750 million was sold for cash, led the way. The other $2.25 billion of the 30-year bond was exchanged for Brady bonds.
The 30-year gobal, the largest ever from an emerging market country, was trading Monday at 365 bps over Treasuries, 30 basis points tighter than its launch price.
Also last week, Brazil placed its 20-year 500 billion Eurolira bond ZYBB.

Other large deals included Banco do Brasil's $400 million two-tranche deal. Each tranche was $200 million, with one carrying a 10-year maturity ZYDJ and the other a five-year maturity ZYDI. The five-year was priced at 200 bps over and narrowed to a spread of 195 bps.
Investors liked the five-year tranche so much that they were seen moving into it and out of Brazil's 8.875 percent global due 2001 ZQ4P, which widened to 160 bps from 148 bps.

BRAZILIAN BRADY BONDS - boosted last week by local issues like the swap/global bond deal and Congressional approval of a controversial re-election bill - were seen returning to a U.S. Treasury-driven focus.
"There was a feel-good factor after the re-election issue was resolved, but people don't have great expectations about the (economic) reform drive," said a Brady trader in New York.

The trader was referring to Brasilia's plans to secure the macroeconomic gains over the past two years with constitutional reforms aimed at slashing government spending and removing bureacratic hurdles to growth.
The reforms have been bogged down in Congress.
